world.title: 卡库亚针问题的最小转向区域
world.posterTitle: 单位线段可以在任意小面积内转向
world.posterHook: 最笨的办法是原地转一圈；更聪明的办法是贴着一条三尖形轨道滑过去。答案是：地方可以几乎为零——但再小也不能瘪成一条线。
world.posterSource: 三尖内摆线 · 挂谷集 · 王虹–Zahl
world.question: 桌上有一根针要掉头，最少需要多大一块地方？
world.hook: 先看针贴着弯曲轨道滑完 180°，再把要求升级成「每个方向都要有一根完整针」——面积竟能几乎为零；但王虹证明：它再小，也瘪不成一条线。
world.payoff: 「每个方向都能躺下一根完整针」的区域叫挂谷集。弯曲的三尖轨道是一个漂亮例子；还可以切成细条再拼，面积想多小有多小。真正的挂谷猜想问另一面：它能不能瘪成更低维的一堆线？王虹与 Zahl（2025）证明三维情形：不能。我们演示的是含义，不是 127 页证明。

en.title: The minimum turning region in the Kakeya needle problem
en.posterTitle: A unit segment can turn inside a region of arbitrarily small area
en.posterHook: The clumsy way is to spin in place; a smarter way is to slide along a three-cusped track. The area can shrink to almost nothing—but it still cannot flatten into a single line.
en.question: A needle on a table needs to turn around—how little room does it need?
en.hook: First watch the needle slide 180° along a curved track, then raise the bar to “a full needle in every direction”—the area can go almost to zero, yet Wang proved it can never flatten into lines.
en.payoff: A region that can hold a full unit needle in every direction is a Kakeya set. The three-cusped track is a beautiful example; thinner strips can make the area as small as you like. The real conjecture asks the flip side—can it collapse into a lower-dimensional bundle of lines? Wang and Zahl (2025) proved the three-dimensional case: no. This world shows what that means, not the 127-page proof.
